title: Abell 3827
caption: The central galaxy of the cluster Abell 3827, imaged by the Gemini South telescope
celestial: Abell 3827 · constellation Indus · about z=0.097 (redshift) away (source figure)
credit: R. Carrasco et al., International Gemini Observatory/AURA

recognition.text: Official NSF NOIRLab / Gemini press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: At the centre of this Gemini South view of the galaxy cluster Abell 3827 sits a huge galaxy, ESO 146-IG 005, surrounded by its cluster companions. Within it are the remains of at least four galactic nuclei that the big galaxy is in the process of 'digesting'.

Out to a distance of about 1.5 billion light-years, this central galaxy is believed to outweigh every other in our local universe. Giant galaxies at the centres of clusters can grow by swallowing smaller galaxies that fall toward them, and the leftover nuclei here are traces of such meals still under way.

The image covers approximately 5 by 5 arcminutes of sky and was made with Gemini South's Multi-Object Spectrograph, in Chile. Travis Rector of the University of Alaska Anchorage combined and processed the g-, r- and i-band images into the colour composite. The cluster, in the direction of Indus, has a redshift of 0.097.

understand.summary: Taken in visible light with the Gemini Multi-Object Spectrograph on Gemini South through g, r and i filters; the colour mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: The long exposure gathers far more light than the eye, revealing the faint remnants of swallowed galaxies.
